steps.body: Two mistakes break a count: skipping a toy, and counting a toy twice. Skipping makes the answer too small; repeating makes it too big.
steps.narration: Two mistakes break a count: skipping a toy, and counting a toy twice. Skipping makes the answer too small; repeating makes it too big.

widget.prompt: Count 6 buttons — one counter each, none skipped, none twice.

commonCounts.feedback: One button was skipped; a skipped button leaves the count one short.
One button was counted twice; a repeat pushes the count one too high.

widget.missFeedback: Slow down: touch each button once, saying one number per touch.
widget.successFeedback: Six counters for six buttons — nothing skipped, nothing doubled.

predict.prompt: Counting a toy twice makes the answer…
predict.reveal: A repeated toy takes two numbers, so the last number said runs past the true amount.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch no skip.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch no skip.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: Ravi counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 8, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 8; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 8.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 8.

widget.prompt: Sam counts 5 blocks but says only four numbers. What happened?

options.label: One block was skipped
options.feedback: Correct — saying four count words for five blocks leaves one block without a number.

options.label: One block was repeated
options.feedback: Repeating a block would make the spoken count too large, not too small.

options.label: The count ran backward
options.feedback: Counting backward can still pair one word with each block; the missing word shows a skip.

options.label: Four is close enough
options.feedback: A count must be exact; one of the five blocks did not receive a count word.

widget.prompt: Start at 4. Hop forward 3 times by 1. Where do you land?

commonLandings.feedback: 6 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
8 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 4 to land on 7.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 4 and count on 3: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 4 and 3 more is 7 — each hop says the next counting number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — count all 3 hops, one number per hop, to reach 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after exactly 3 hops, on 7.
